title: Vasquez rejects image-alone adoration as superstitious—must co-venerate the prototype
source_text: XLII. Quidam, ut Gabriel Vasquez, hunc adorationis modum tanquam superstitiosum & stultum rejiciunt, quia, videlicet, stultum est creaturam rationalem se subjicere creaturae irrationali, & servam illius sese exhibere. Adeoque pertendunt imaginem per se, sine prototypo, vel ab eo separatam adorari licite non posse: Non solum quia necesse est propter exemplar, tanquam propter rationem remotam, sicut legatum propter Regem, imaginem coli: sed quia qui imaginem adorat, in ea quoque, & per eam, exemplar, ut terminum, & materiam proximam venerationis, venerari debet. Quae sunt verba Gabrielis Vasquez, tomo primo in tertiam Thomae disputat. 108. cap. 3.
pass_a_gloss: Some, as Gabriel Vasquez, reject this mode of adoration as superstitious and foolish, because, namely, it is foolish for a rational creature to subject itself to an irrational creature, and to exhibit itself as its servant. And so they maintain that an image per se, without the prototype, or separated from it, cannot lawfully be adored: Not only because it is necessary that the image be cultivated on account of the exemplar, as on account of a remote reason, as a legate on account of the King: but because he who adores the image ought also in it, and through it, to venerate the exemplar as terminus and proximate matter of veneration. Which are the words of Gabriel Vasquez, in the first tome on the third part of Thomas, disputation 108, chapter 3.
pass_b_english: Vasquez brands image-alone adoration superstitious: a rational creature must not subject itself to an irrational one.
An image without its prototype cannot lawfully be adored; the adorant must also venerate the exemplar in and through the image as terminus.
Cited: Vasquez on ST III, disp. 108, c. 3.

choices.why: Vasquez requires the exemplar in that role.
